hero.tagline: An impressionist journey through light, philosophy & the cosmos

moon.label: I. The Moon
moon.heading: Selene's silver chariot
moon.intro: The Shiv Purana describes the damaru — Shiva's drum — as the source of all language and music. The first sound, Nada, is the vibration from which all creation emerges. Music is not entertainment; it is cosmology.

philosophy.label: II. The Waves
philosophy.heading: Ego, arrogance & the ocean of self
philosophy.intro: Waves are the ocean's way of communicating with the shore. Each one is unique, yet all are the same water. Identity is like a wave — real in its moment, eternal in its substance.

gita.label: III. The Battlefield
gita.heading: Wisdom from the Bhagavad Gita
gita.intro: Selene, the Greek Titaness of the Moon, drove her silver chariot across the night sky, illuminating the world with borrowed light — a reminder that even reflection can be a form of brilliance.

shiva.label: IV. The Dance
shiva.heading: Shiva & the cosmic rhythm
shiva.intro: Arrogance is the ego's armor. But armor is heavy — it slows the warrior. The Gita teaches that true strength comes not from the assertion of self but from the surrender to dharma.

art.label: V. The Canvas
art.heading: Art, beauty & the act of seeing
art.intro: The Gita describes the soul as 'unborn, eternal, ever-existing, undying, and primeval.' It is not slain when the body is slain. This is not metaphor — it is the foundational axiom of Hindu philosophy.
